extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, USPTO OED staff, disciplinary counsel, and attorneys subject to USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Procedure and standards for transferring a registered patent attorney to disability inactive status under 37 C.F.R. § 11.29, including notice, opportunity to respond, publication, and the practical effects and restrictions of the transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for reciprocal transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer to disability inactive status may be ordered by the USPTO based on a reciprocal proceeding when a state court (here, the Supreme Court of Colorado) has transferred the attorney to disability inactive status regarding the practice of law in that jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites the state decision (People v. William R. Hyde, 19PDJ035) as the basis for the USPTO's reciprocal action; the OED Director files a Request for Reciprocal Transfer to Disability Inactive Status pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.29.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Order to Respondent (service requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.29 must be mailed to the Respondent (here mailed by certified mail with receipt numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document shows specific certified mail receipt numbers as evidence of service; the Notice provides the respondent an opportunity to file a response within the statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond / response period
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is provided an opportunity to file, within thirty (30) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal transfer to disability inactive status based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's timely response (here, an email stating consent) is considered; if respondent does not contest, the proceeding may be resolved without disputed factual issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for opposing transfer (per 37 C.F.R. § 11.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice informs Respondent they may oppose the transfer based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order does not enumerate the § 11.29 grounds on-page, but explicitly ties the respondent's right to oppose to the statutory/regulatory reasons set forth in § 11.29.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for decision when uncontested (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Respondent does not contest the transfer, the OED Director (or delegate) may determine that there is 'no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.29(d)' and find transfer appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order concludes that in light of Respondent's decision not to contest, transfer to disability inactive status is appropriate and ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of transfer on authorization to practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer to disability inactive status precludes the Respondent from the practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for an indefinite period until further order of the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice language states: 'While on disability inactive status, Mr. Hyde shall not be authorized to practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice of Transfer to Disability Inactive Status in the Official Gazette identifying the registrant and summarizing the transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order provides an example notice text that includes the attorney's name, registration number, the state action citation, the effect on practice before the USPTO, and cites the statutory/regulatory authority (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.29). It also references public availability at OED's FOIA Reading Room (https://foiadocuments.uspto.gov/oed/).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the transfer and the reasons for the transfer to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly orders the OED Director to provide these notices as part of the transfer process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's duties while on disability inactive status (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order references § 11.58 but does not list the duties on-page; compliance with that regulatory provision is required as a condition of the transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer Numbers and USPTO electronic accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s), if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents the Respondent from practicing before the USPTO through previously associated customer numbers or electronic accounts while on disability inactive status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall he have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order makes clear these are continuing prohibitions tied to the disability inactive status and reinstatement condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citation for action
rubrics_metrics.description: The transfer action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders and notices should cite the statutory and regulatory authority for the transfer; this citation is included in the sample Official Gazette notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary/transfer decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions and decisions regarding transfer to disability inactive status are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order provides the FOIA Reading Room URL (https://foiadocuments.uspto.gov/oed/) as the place where such documents are published for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director files a Request for reciprocal transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The process begins with the OED Director filing a 'Request for Reciprocal Transfer to Disability Inactive Status Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.29' requesting that the Director of the USPTO transfer the Respondent to disability inactive status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Request references the state disciplinary action and initiates the USPTO reciprocal process; the Notice and Order follows the filing of that Request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent consent as dispositive
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent expressly consents to transfer (e.g., via email stating 'I consent to being transferred to disability inactive status'), the Office may proceed to order the transfer without further contested proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order relied on the Respondent's consent to find no genuine issue of material fact and to order transfer.
